comparison: Perfect agreement. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find claims C4, C6, C21, and C128 about C-terminal tagging effects on emerin trafficking to be well-supported. Reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as a 'valuable finding' with 'solid evidence' for tag-induced artifacts.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations support claims C56-C63 regarding LAP2β showing similar trafficking mechanisms to emerin. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings as part of the 'thorough dissection' without raising concerns.

Agreement on uncertainty. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find claims C65-C67 about COPI interactions supported by mass spectrometry data but uncertain regarding mechanism. Authors acknowledge unexpected lack of RXR-dependence; reviewers do not explicitly validate the mechanistic interpretation.

Strong agreement. Both evaluations support claims C7, C20, C45-C49 about RXR motif limiting trafficking. OpenEval finds evidence from deletion/mutation experiments; peer reviewers explicitly accept 'an ER retention sequence' as contributing to trafficking mechanism without challenge.

Strong agreement with partial overlap. Both support TMD hydrophobicity claims (C5, C18, C37-C39, C96). OpenEval includes additional claims (C33, C40-C43) about TMD swap experiments. Peer reviewer explicitly states 'increased TMD hydrophobicity contribute[s] to Emerin's trafficking' with solid evidence.

Strong agreement. Both support claims C16, C79, C80, C82, C129 about differential N- vs C-terminal tagging effects in DICE iPSC system. Peer reviewers acknowledge the comparison and accept 'solid evidence' for tag-induced artifacts. OpenEval also includes C81, C84, C85.

Strong agreement. Both support claims C72-C74, C77-C78 about DICE iPSC validation experiments showing conserved mechanisms. Peer reviewers do not challenge these findings; OpenEval also includes C75-C76. Both view this as supporting generalizability across cell types.

Strong agreement. Both support claims C29-C32 about domain deletion experiments. OpenEval also includes C28. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings as part of the broader TMD-dependent trafficking mechanism that they explicitly endorse.

Strong agreement. Both support claim C130 about tag orientation affecting trafficking as a cautionary conclusion. Peer reviewers explicitly endorse this as 'a caution regarding placement of tags' and 'a warning to epitope-tagging approaches.' Peer review also addresses C131.

Disagreement on certainty. OpenEval supports claims C103-C108 about biogenesis pathways and ERES colocalization. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly identifies this as uncertain, stating the biogenesis pathway 'might confound some interpretations' and 'remains to be determined.' Partial claim overlap (C103-C104, C107-C108).

Strong agreement. Both support claims C86-C88 about bulk flow mechanism based on temperature block and ERES experiments. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly validates Sec31A colocalization data supporting secretory pathway entry. OpenEval also includes C89-C90; peer review also addresses C105-C106.

Agreement on uncertainty. Both find claims C17, C93-C95 about untagged emerin trafficking uncertain due to assay limitations. OpenEval notes negative results may reflect sensitivity issues; peer reviewers note authors acknowledge data were 'considerably noisier.' OpenEval also includes C131.

OpenEval supports claims C53-C54 about combinatorial mutagenesis showing TMD-RXR hierarchy. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these specific claims about rescue experiments are not explicitly discussed by reviewers.
